items.title: Simon Willison gets a coding agent to render 3D scenes in Blender via a reusable skill
items.summary_en: Independent researcher/engineer Simon Willison documented using ChatGPT's Codex mode (macOS) to drive the open-source 3D tool Blender through natural-language prompts, iterating a 'pelican riding a bicycle' render across three rounds (roughly 2m39s, 3m51s, and 5m59s) and having the agent produce a reusable 'Blender Local' skill file so future scenes can be generated with one instruction. He followed up days later with a browser-based .blend file viewer built the same way.

items.title: Autonomous 'AI Scientist' agents claim a new best score on Karpathy's NanoChat speed-training benchmark
items.summary_en: A blog post from rekursiv.ai reports that a team of autonomous AI research agents ('auto-auto-research') reached a mean of 0.887791 bits-per-byte across 10 seeds on Andrej Karpathy's community NanoChat benchmark, within a five-minute training budget on a single B200 GPU. The post frames this as evidence that AI systems can now meaningfully self-optimize small-scale language-model training loops with minimal human tuning, though the claim comes from the team's own writeup rather than an independent benchmark authority.
